question.prompt:
A region is bounded by semicircular arcs constructed on the sides of a square whose sides measure \(\tfrac{2}{\pi},\) as shown. What is the perimeter of this region?

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_10B_Q06_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The square's sides lie inside the shaded region, so the perimeter consists only of the four semicircular arcs. Each square side is the diameter of one semicircle. A semicircular arc has half the circumference of its full circle, so each arc has length
\[
\frac12\pi\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)=1.
\]
Adding the four arc lengths gives a perimeter of \(4\), choice \(\boxed{D}\).
solutions.title: Half of each circumference
